I’m 46 years old, got only primary schooling, and I’ve been farming these 6 mu in Quzhou my whole life. I don’t trust book learning much—what I know comes from my father, from my own eyes, and from watching the neighbors. Old Wang down the road has good wheat every year, so if he does something, I pay attention.

It’s early spring now. My winter wheat went in last October, same as always. I ploughed the field in the fall and sowed an improved variety my cousin gave me—nothing fancy, but it’s reliable. The wheat is greening up and looks all right, though a bit thin in one corner. I’ll irrigate three times in total: I already did the winter irrigation, and now I’ll water at jointing and again at grain filling. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting—about 100 jin per mu—and I’ll topdress with urea when the wheat starts jointing. I figure that’s about 18 jin of pure nitrogen per mu all told. I thought about cutting back after fertilizer prices went up, but two years ago I tried less and the yield dropped badly. I’d rather waste a little money than risk going hungry. I’ll spray herbicide once and insecticide once or twice if I see aphids.

For summer, I’ll plant maize on the same 6 mu right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There’s barely a week between harvest and planting, so I’ll use rotary tillage—no time for deep ploughing. I buy hybrid seed every year, usually whatever the shop in town recommends. I’ll put down one basal dressing of compound fertilizer, about 16 jin of nitrogen per mu, and irrigate twice if July is dry. One pesticide spray for weeds, and maybe another for corn borers if they show up. I’ve thought about cotton, but my wife works in the factory and I can’t manage the picking alone. Wheat-maize is what I know, and it feeds my family.
